briefdescription.para: Native implementation of "createCertificateImpl(String path, Password pwd, String name, String dName)".

detaileddescription.para: For provider "self", replaces: keytool -delete -alias <name> -keystore <path> -storepass <pwd> keytool -genkeypair -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 90 -alias <name> -dname <dName> -storetype PKCS12 -keystore <path> -storepass <pwd> The Java implementation uses java.security.KeyPairGenerator (RSA, 2048-bit) and BouncyCastle's X509v3CertificateBuilder with SHA256WithRSA — the same JDK crypto primitives that keytool uses internally. The resulting PKCS12 keystore entry is interchangeable with keytool output.

For providers "certbot"/"certbot-staging", replaces the multistep native flow: openssl genpkey openssl req certbot certonly --webroot openssl pkcs12 -export keytool -importkeystore The Java implementation uses acme4j to speak the ACME protocol directly, eliminating all intermediate files and format conversions. Challenge files are written to the same .challenge/.well-known/acme-challenge/ directory that certbot's webroot mode used, so the platform's AcmeChallenge web service works unchanged.

memberdef.name: createCertificateWithAcme

briefdescription.para: Create a certificate using the ACME protocol (Let's Encrypt) via acme4j.

detaileddescription.para: Replaces the old five-step native flow (openssl genpkey → openssl req → certbot certonly → openssl pkcs12 -export → keytool -importkeystore) with a single in-process ACME interaction. The domain keypair and certificate chain are stored directly into the keystore without intermediate PEM/PKCS12 temp files, which is both simpler and more secure (no unencrypted private key written to disk).

Polling uses acme4j's waitForCompletion(Duration) which respects the server's Retry-After header, rather than the old approach of blocking on process.waitFor(300, SECONDS) while certbot polled internally.

memberdef.name: processHttpChallenges

briefdescription.para: Process HTTP-01 challenges for each pending authorization.

detaileddescription.para: Writes challenge token files to .challenge/.well-known/acme-challenge/ — the same directory layout that certbot's --webroot --webroot-path mode used. The platform's AcmeChallenge web service serves these files at the path that Let's Encrypt expects (/.well-known/acme-challenge/{token}).

Native implementation of "revokeCertificateImpl(String path, Password pwd, String name)".

detaileddescription.para: Replaces the old native flow: certbot revoke --config-dir <certs>/config --cert-name <name> --reason unspecified keytool -delete -alias <name> -keystore <path> -storepass <pwd> The old certbot revocation used the stored account key from its config directory. The Java implementation uses domain-key revocation (RFC 8555 §7.6) — extracting the domain keypair from the keystore, which is more robust because it doesn't depend on certbot's external config state.

memberdef.name: revokeWithAcme

briefdescription.para: Revoke a certificate using the ACME protocol via acme4j.

detaileddescription.para: Uses domain-key-authenticated revocation: the private key that signed the CSR is extracted from the keystore and used to prove ownership to the ACME server. This is one of two revocation mechanisms defined in RFC 8555 §7.6 (the other being account-key revocation). We use domain-key revocation because the account keypair is ephemeral (generated fresh per certificate request) and not persisted, whereas the domain key is always in the keystore alongside the certificate.

briefdescription.para: Native implementation of "invokeCreateSymmetricKeyImpl(String path, Password pwd, String name)".

detaileddescription.para: Replaces: keytool -delete -alias <name> -keystore <path> -storepass <pwd> keytool -genseckey -keyalg AES -keysize 256 -alias <name> -storetype PKCS12 -keystore <path> -storepass <pwd> Uses javax.crypto.KeyGenerator#getInstance(String) with AES/256 — the same JDK API that keytool's -genseckey uses internally. The resulting SecretKeyEntry in the PKCS12 keystore is identical in format.

briefdescription.para: Native implementation of "invokeCreatePasswordImpl(String path, Password pwd, String name, String pwdValue)".

detaileddescription.para: Replaces: keytool -delete -alias <name> -keystore <path> -storepass <pwd> echo <pwdValue> | keytool -importpass -alias <name> -storetype PKCS12 -keystore <path> -storepass <pwd> Uses javax.crypto.SecretKeyFactory#getInstance(String) with "PBE" to create a PBE secret key from the password value, then stores it as a SecretKeyEntry — the same internal representation that keytool's -importpass produces.

briefdescription.para: Native implementation of the xRTCertificateManager.x service.

detaileddescription.para: It uses pure Java APIs (JDK crypto, BouncyCastle, acme4j) that produce byte-for-byte compatible PKCS12 keystore entries. Keystores created by this implementation can be read by keytool and openssl, and vice versa — verified by KeyStoreCompatibilityTest.
